title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and templates for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and people managers who run the day-to-day people processes.
table_of_contents:
1) Hiring process overview
2) Interview panel & scorecard guidelines
3) Offer approval and onboarding flow
4) 30/60/90 new hire plan and manager checklist
5) Performance & feedback cycle
6) Manager responsibilities and best practices
7) Forms, templates, and links
hiring_process_overview:
Purpose: Provide a predictable, fair, and efficient hiring experience that balances candidate experience with quality-of-hire metrics.

Hiring targets and SLAs:
- Time to first-screen: 3 business days (target)
- Time to onsite/loop: 14 calendar days (target)
- Time to offer: 28 calendar days (target)
- Time to hire (accept + start): 35-45 calendar days (target)
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70%

Key roles and ownership:
- Hiring manager: defines role requirements, owns final decision and hiring timeline.
- Recruiter: owns candidate sourcing, coordination, and offer negotiation.
- Interview panel: evaluates candidates against the scorecard.
- People Ops: owners of policy, equity offers, background checks, and compliance.

Process overview (high level):
1. Requisition approval: Hiring manager opens req in Workday/Greenhouse with role spec, compensation band, and justification. People Ops must approve the req before active sourcing.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter sources and conducts 15-30m screen; hiring manager approves moving to interview loop.
3. Interview loop: 4-6 interviews across functional, systems, and culture fit. Use standardized scorecard.
4. Debrief & decision: Panel meets within 48 hours of loop completion. Hiring manager closes decision and communicates to recruiter.
5. Offer & negotiation: Recruiter builds offer packet; People Ops approves equity and signing bonus.
6. Background check & preboarding: Initiate background check; create new-hire packet in HRIS.
7. Start & onboarding: Manager follows 30/60/90 plan and confirms role readiness.

Diversity & fairness:
- All job postings must include an inclusive statement and minimum required qualifications only.
- All interview panels must include at least one trained interviewer who completed unconscious-bias training in the last 12 months (exceptions require People Ops sign-off).
- Use structured interview rubrics for every hire.

Escalation rules:
- If a requisition is stalled >21 days without a pipeline update, People Ops will flag to the hiring manager and the recruiter for a remediation plan.
- Compensation exceptions outside published bands require VP People Ops approval.
interview_panel_guidelines:
Objective: Ensure consistent, evidence-based evaluations.

Panel composition and roles:
- Hiring manager: owns final calibration and should interview at least 1 candidate in the loop.
- Technical lead or peer: evaluates role-specific skills.
- Systems/infra/ops (when applicable): assesses reliability and operational considerations.
- Cross-functional partner: evaluates collaboration and communication skills.

Scorecard (standard fields):
- Role fit (0-5)
- Technical ability / craft (0-5)
- Problem solving & design (0-5)
- Communication & collaboration (0-5)
- Ownership & bias for action (0-5)
- Culture & values alignment (0-5)
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / On hold / Pass

Scoring guidelines (short):
- 5 = Exceptional: clearly exceeds expectations and would add immediate impact.
- 3 = Meets expectations: capable and reliable but needs development to excel.
- 1 = Insufficient: significant gaps; additional evidence required.

Interviewer expectations and best practices:
- Use the same rubric for every candidate for this role.
- Ask open-ended, job-relevant questions and probe for specific examples.
- Avoid hypotheticals that are not representative of day-to-day work.
- Document evidence: each score must be accompanied by 1-2 bullets of evidence.
- Return feedback within 48 hours of the interview. Late feedback must be flagged and reconciled before final decision.

Debrief meeting template (agenda):
1. Quick summary of each interviewer’s scores (5-10 minutes).
2. Discuss major strengths and risk areas (10-15 minutes).
3. Reach a consensus recommendation and identify post-offer concerns (10 minutes).
4. Assign follow-ups (reference checks, technical homework, etc.) (5 minutes).
offer_and_onboarding:
Offer approval flow:
1. Hiring manager provides target compensation and rationale to Recruiter.
2. Recruiter prepares offer packet with base, bonus, equity, and potential sign-on.
3. People Ops verifies band alignment, equity allocation, and compliance (48-hour SLA).
4. Recruiter extends offer verbally and follows up by email with written offer.
5. Candidate accepts; Recruiter opens background check and initiates preboarding tasks.

Preboarding checklist (to be completed before start date):
- Background check initiated and passed.
- Employment paperwork uploaded to HRIS (W-4, direct deposit, regional equivalents).
- Equipment order placed (laptop, monitor, dock) and shipping scheduled.
- Manager connects with new hire to confirm first-day logistics and team intro.
- New hire invited to essential Slack channels, calendar invites, and Confluence pages.

Onboarding logistics and first day timeline:
- Day 0 (before start): IT and People Ops confirm equipment and access.
- Day 1 morning: Welcome, HR orientation (benefits, payroll), and account provisioning.
- Day 1 afternoon: Team welcome, role overview, 30/60/90 plan review.
- Week 1: Technical setup, essential trainings, initial project assignment (small scope).

Role of People Ops during onboarding:
- Ensure compliance tasks are completed and provide benefits orientation.
- Run the new-hire survey at day 7 and day 30 to capture early signals.
- Maintain the central onboarding checklist and route escalations for missing items.
onboarding_90_day_plan:
Purpose: Provide clarity for the new hire and manager on expectations, success metrics, and integration milestones.

30-day goals (orientation and ramp basics):
- Complete required compliance and security trainings.
- Complete initial production-facing technical onboarding and local environment setup.
- Deliver a small scoped task that exercises the core skill set.
- Meet with top 8 cross-functional partners to understand stakeholder needs.

60-day goals (contribution and ownership):
- Take on a larger project with clear deliverables and a measurable outcome.
- Begin owning an operational or code area with guidance from the manager.
- Present progress to the team and collect feedback.

90-day goals (independence and impact):
- Fully own at least one component or feature area end-to-end.
- Demonstrate ability to plan, estimate, and communicate progress.
- Receive formal 90-day check-in from manager and People Ops.

Manager checklist (pre-start to 90 days):
- Pre-start: Create onboarding schedule, enable accounts, order equipment, and assign a buddy.
- Week 1: Daily check-ins first 3 days, then thrice-weekly.
- Week 2-4: Weekly one-on-one focused on ramp blockers and feedback.
- Month 2: Bi-weekly 1:1s and results-focused reviews.
- Month 3: Formal 90-day review with calibration to peer expectations.

New hire buddy program:
- Assign a buddy from day 0 for social integration, quick technical questions, and culture norms.
- Buddy responsibilities: weekly syncs for first month and available for ad-hoc questions.
performance_and_feedback_cycle:
Rhythm: Redwood runs a quarterly performance and feedback cycle with an annual calibration and promotion window. The cycle balances frequent coaching with documented reviews.

Quarterly cycle elements:
- Ongoing 1:1 coaching (recommended cadence: weekly for ICs in first 6 months; ongoing bi-weekly thereafter).
- Mid-quarter check-in: informal pulse to evaluate progress on goals.
- End-of-quarter review: written self-assessment + manager assessment.
- Calibration: manager peer calibration across teams to normalize expectations and leveling.

Ratings and expectations (summary):
- Level 1 — Meets (Meets expectations): consistently delivers role responsibilities and contributes reliably.
- Level 2 — Exceeds (High performer): delivers beyond role expectations and drives cross-team impact.
- Level 3 — Exceptional (Standout): sustained, outsized impact and leadership without title change.
- Development needed: performance below expectations; manager and People Ops produce an improvement plan.

Feedback best practices for managers:
- Make feedback timely, specific, and tied to observable behavior.
- Use the "situation-behavior-impact" (SBI) method for clarity.
- Document coaching conversations and follow up with a written summary.
- For performance concerns, escalate to People Ops early to design a support plan (30-60-90 improvement plan).

Promotion and compensation review windows:
- Promotion review: twice yearly (March and September windows). Managers must submit promotion packets 4 weeks before calibration.
- Compensation review: annual review in December; ad-hoc adjustments for retention risks require People Ops approval.
manager_responsibilities:
Overview: Managers are primary operators of people development, performance management, and role clarity. This section outlines core expectations.

Core responsibilities:
- Hiring: partner with recruiter and own final hiring decision and onboarding plan.
- Onboarding: create 30/60/90 goals, assign buddy, and track ramp progress.
- Performance: conduct regular 1:1s, document check-ins, and run formal reviews on schedule.
- Development: create career plans, provide stretch opportunities, and support promotions.
- Wellbeing & retention: monitor workload, encourage time off, and escalate burnout risks.

Operational cadence recommended:
- Weekly team stand-up (status & blockers).
- Weekly 1:1 with each direct report (30-45 minutes).
- Monthly skip-levels or AMAs.
- Quarterly career calibration with People Ops.

Manager checklist for performance concerns (short):
1. Document specific incidents and data points.
2. Have an initial coaching conversation using SBI.
3. If no improvement in 2-4 weeks, set a documented performance improvement plan (PIP) with measurable outcomes.
4. Engage People Ops before issuing a formal PIP or termination.

Training & enablement for managers:
- All managers must complete the Redwood Manager Fundamentals course within 90 days of promotion/hire.
- Recommended additional training: feedback techniques, bias mitigation, and compensation calibration workshops.
notes_and_next_steps: This doc is owned by People Ops. Review cadence: annual review in Q4 and ad-hoc updates after major policy changes (comp bands, region-specific legal updates). Request changes by creating a pull request in the People Ops docs repo or contacting the owner. For localized variants (country-specific onboarding), maintain a short localized appendix linked from this page.
